title: Melon de Bourgogne
description: The grape of Muscadet: light, crisp and saline, made richer by ageing on its lees.
L: Melon de Bourgogne, often just Melon, gives light, very dry whites with lemon, green apple, pear, white flowers and a saline, mineral note. Acidity is high, alcohol moderate, often 12% or less; Muscadet is legally capped at 12% for most wines. It's neutral in aroma, which makes lees ageing important.

As its name says, Melon came from Burgundy. It's a cross of Pinot Noir and Gouais Blanc, a sibling of Chardonnay. After the harsh winter of 1709 killed many vines near Nantes, growers replanted with frost-resistant Melon. It became the grape of Muscadet, near the Loire's mouth. Burgundy later banned it.
Why was Melon planted near Nantes?
It survived the harsh winter of 1709
After the 1709 freeze, frost-resistant Melon replaced lost vines.

Look for very pale colour, a subtle nose of lemon, apple and sea air, and a light, crisp, saline palate. Lees-aged versions add bread and a slight creaminess, and sometimes a tiny spritz. Compared with Pinot Grigio, it's more saline and mineral.
Melon de Bourgogne is a sibling of Chardonnay.
Yes. Both are crosses of Pinot Noir and Gouais Blanc.
Melon gives light, crisp, saline whites
It came from Burgundy and replaced vines near Nantes after 1709

Melon grows almost only in the Pays Nantais, near Nantes, where the Loire meets the Atlantic. Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, the largest and most important appellation, sits south-east of Nantes. Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire and Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu are smaller. The climate is maritime: mild, damp, with sea breezes.

Since 2011, Muscadet has recognised crus communaux, village crus, with specific soils and longer lees ageing, from 17 months to several years. Examples include Clisson, on granite, Gorges, on gabbro, and Le Pallet, on gneiss and gabbro. They show Melon's capacity for complex, age-worthy wines.
Match each cru to its soil.
Look for a cru communal name on a Muscadet label. These wines spend much longer on their lees and show how serious Melon can be.
Village crus with specific soils and long lees ageing
They require specific soils and extended lees ageing.
Melon grows in the Pays Nantais, mainly Sèvre et Maine
The climate is maritime and mild
Crus communaux, since 2011, show its complexity

Muscadet sur lie stays on its fine lees, the dead yeast, through winter until bottling in spring. This adds bread and yeasty notes, a creamier texture and protection against oxidation, plus a slight spritz from retained CO2. It gives a neutral grape more depth and character.

Muscadet is the classic oyster wine: its high acidity, low alcohol and saline edge match shellfish perfectly. It also suits mussels, clams, crab, grilled sardines and beurre blanc, Nantes' butter sauce. Serve at 7 to 9 degrees. Most is best within three years; crus communaux age 10 years or more.
What does sur lie ageing add to Muscadet?
Bread notes, creaminess and a slight spritz
Lees contact adds texture and depth.
Muscadet is one of the best-value white wines in France. A good sur lie with a dozen oysters is a classic French pleasure.

Muscadet is made from the Muscat grape.
